why:
rcl's "set THIS logger's level", and the one member of `rcl_log_levels_*` that is a capability rather than allocation bookkeeping. The SHAPE is declined with the rest of the family (`c:log_levels_*`): it takes an `rcl_log_levels_t *` — a heap-allocated growable array of (name, severity) pairs carrying an `rcl_allocator_t`, populated from `--ros-args --log-level` — and we have no allocator and no argv (RFC-0045). The CAPABILITY inside it is not declined and is no longer missing.

CORRECTION (2026-09-13). This row was a `gap` reading: "C and C++ have NO way to reach it: `<rclc/log.h>` exposes only `rclc_log_emit`, `rclc_log_emit_fmt`, `rclc_log_init` and `rclc_log_default_logger`, and there is no `rclc_logger_set_level` / `rclc_logger_get_level` on the `rclc_logger_t` handle." Every clause of that is now false. phase-417 W4.d shipped `rclc_logger_set_level` / `rclc_logger_get_level` / `rclc_logger_is_enabled` beside `rclc_log_get_logger` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/log.h`), and the C++ half landed as `cpp:Logger::set_level` on 2026-09-13. The row is re-verdicted rather than deleted because rcl's TYPE is still declined and a reader arriving from `rcl_log_levels_add_logger_setting` needs to be told where the capability went: `c:logger_set_level`, `c:logger_get_level`, `c:logger_is_enabled`.

The old row also recorded that `examples/linux/c/logging/src/main.c`'s file comment claimed a threshold helper the file did not contain. That is the example's to fix and is not this row's subject; the accessor it described now exists.
